newsitem.title: USA: Nine West gives further SEC probe details.
newsitem.headline: Nine West gives further SEC probe details.

text.p: Nine West Group said Wednesday a Securities and Exchange Commission investigation of its revenue-booking policies is focused on businesses it acquired from U.S. Shoe and that it involves the wholesale side of its business.
It said it learned on May 1 that the probe had become a formal investigation as of April 10.

"We have no idea at this point in time when it will be completed," said Robert Galvin, Nine West's chief financial officer during a conference call. "This investigation has had no impact on our business at this point in time," he added.
Galvin said "as far as we're aware" the SEC probe deals with accounting practices during 1995. Nine West does not expect the investigation to have a material impact on it finances, he added.
"Based on what we know the issues to be today, we are saying we don't believe it will have a material adverse effect on the company," he said.

Nine West acquired the footwear division of Cincinnati-based U.S. Shoe Corp in May of 1995. Since the acquisition, Nine West has not changed its accounting policies, and it does not expect to restate earnings.
"We believe we have continued to look at policies and practivies to esure that any questions will not be ongoing issues," Galvin said.

Stamford, Conn.,-based Nine West, a retailer and manufacturer of women's shoes, is cooperating with the SEC, Galvin said. The probe has not reached the stage of negotiations, and the company is not aware of what triggered the SEC's decision to make the investigation a formal one.
"There is nothing that we're aware of that required it to go from informal to formal," Galvin said. Nine West's brands include Enzo Angiolini, Easy Spirit, Bandolino and Evan Picone.

Nine West, which employs about 13,000, operates 1,061 of its own retail stores. After its acquisition of U.S. Shoe's footwear group, it had five domestic footwear manufacturing facilities but has closed two of them since April.
Nine West had said in its annual report that it planned to close three of the factories and reconfigure or close the other two to cut costs and beef up global sourcing.

The company's shares rose about nine percent Wednesday after sliding about 18 percent Tuesday when it filed an amended annual report with the SEC that disclosed the investigation. The stock was up $3 to $35.50 on the New York Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.
Analysts said they were relieved to learn the focus of the probe appears to be accounting policies that were in place when Nine West acquired U.S. Shoe.
On the other hand, Nine West has not overhauled its accounting policies, and a cloud could linger over the company until the full scope of the investigation is known, they said.
"It appears the investigaiton is isolated to 1995," said Jeff Stein of McDonald & Co. "But there's nothing to say the scope of the investigation will not be expanded."
